findings.summary: L1 FLAT (explains itself): 'The manager says it about nine times a night' announces the payoff in advance.
L2 FLAT (sitcom callback): Ryosuke's taiyaki head-or-tail bit in Natsuki's mouth; 'Don't start.' is a canned button.
L3 FLAT (unclear): 'Wednesday.' after 'See you tomorrow' is redundant or undecodable; same sign-off reused at c2_0248.
L4 FLAT (too tidy, placed badly): the 'Again.' note gives the last beat of Natsuki's scene to Nanoha and blurs the note pairing; its meaning depends on a Ch1 setup.
L5 FLAT: rerun of the apron exchange's shape; Takatsuki's topper reads as an intentional burn, off his sheet.
L6 FLAT (generic): 'quiet a room by not raising his voice' is a stock phrase.
L7 FLAT (explains itself, tidy button): 'Nobody laughs. He seems satisfied anyway.' narrates his reaction.
L8 FLAT (off-voice): Rika's dry deflation is on her Never list.
L9 FLAT (unclear): 'she' reads as Rika; the narration also gives away the lost-and-found glasses exchange.
L10 FLAT (off-voice): 'So be afraid.' is Nanoha's deadpan in Natsuki's mouth.
L11 CUT (explains the joke): Rika restates Natsuki's 'There was a head' punchline.
L12 FLAT: spends the repetition device a second time; mock helplessness explains its own joke.
L13 FLAT: 'You're doing great, visual aid.' is the third topper in a row.
L14 FLAT: 'Half a second, I stop to think' pre-empts Kirishima's later line; stiff syntax.
L15 FLAT: narration vouches for the dialogue and states the kinship outright.
L16 FLAT (sitcom quip, off-voice): Kohei's 'You too' flub in the most delicate scene.
L17 FLAT (on-the-nose): 'So I have proof I was there.' states the motive the ending shows.
L18 FLAT (explains itself): justifies her casual invitation; a second retreat follows at c2_0226.
L19 CUT: narration explains the subtext and announces his reply; 'cup filled too full' is writerly.
L20 CUT (too tidy): nearly names the half-date; the bridge scene has three endings.
L21 FLAT (too tidy): punchline structure spells out the sad turn.
L22 FLAT (tidy qualifier): inserted text 'except the last one' walks back 'every time' and blunts the uncanny read.
Scene-level: five of eight scenes close on a neat button.
Scene-level: seven of eight lesson exchanges end on a topper.
Scene-level: stated feelings (L15, L17-L21) cluster on the bridge and interlude, the scenes that need most subtext.
Scene-level: narration repeats or vouches for the dialogue in eight places (L1, L7, L9, L14, L15, L19, L20, L21).
S1: narration reads Natsuki through 'like she's...' twice; about ten similes is a lot for this narrator.
S2: stacked short sentences in narration become a rhythm tic.
S3: Rika's 'scheme' expression on plain questions with no scheme.
S4: expression rules broken (questions without 'curious'; smirk on a non-competitive beat; c2_0160 rule collision).
S5: Rika's chant drops '-kun'; decide and log.
S6: English and Japanese don't match (dropped hesitation).
S7: missing gloss: 'bogu' first appears unglossed at c2_0076; gloss only at c2_0292.
B1: Kohei's 'Mm.' is Nanoha's listed dodge.
Structural note: both of Kohei's walk-home scenes end by cutting to Nanoha, against Ch2's job of pulling the wanting toward even; the Tuesday 'Again.' note doesn't earn its place.
Top fix 1: stop narrating the bridge; one retreat instead of two.
Top fix 2: give Natsuki's jokes back to her own mechanism.
Top fix 3: don't end her Tuesday scene on Nanoha; cut or move the 'Again.' note.
Top fix 4: cut Kohei's 'You too' flub in the catch aftermath.
Top fix 5: thin the lesson's punchlines and remove narration that pre-states lines.

#2: debana setup ('Mostly you don't', 'hardest thing... on purpose') stacks the uncanny above the outline's target.
#3: Akane's 7 pm empty-container photo routine contradicts Ch3 scene 3.1 as outlined.

#7: 'Three nights a week' contradicts the Japanese (three days) and the Sunday day shift.
#8: background doesn't follow him home (container on the kitchen table over bg_restaurant_night; lit window over bg_bridge_dusk).
#9: pilot-notes records the wrong practice session order.
#10: 'one sentence to each of us' but Kirishima says four sentences; scene title too.
#11: ambiguous 'she' reads as Rika wiping the board.
#12: reused Rika sprite shows Monday's clips against the 'different clip every day' [P].
#13: Natsuki's favorite technique (debana) settles an Open item; must be logged [P].
#14: [P] town name SHIRASAWA on box labels may be baked into art.
Story note: reader target says 'Tuesday walk' but 2.1 is at the restaurant.
Story note: chapter map still says 'casual sparring' for Ch2.
C1: stray mid-air drop beside her face reads as a second tear; also in the clip.
I1: Natsuki drawn too tall (about 0.96 of Kohei vs 0.913).

#3: 'she' reads as Rika; only Rika's sprite is on stage.

#5: expressions held past their line.

Her hand is frozen mid-wave while her face falls.

The Chie text and the interlude narration restate the dojo point a second and third time; the text is flat as the third telling.
Both interludes end on the same 'chose not to think about it' beat; starting to feel like a formula.
'[Background: natsuki apartment, night]' is lowercase and placeholder-like.
Natsuki's red hair and green eyes are never acknowledged in the text.
Stricken-face variant keeps the cheerful wave.
Her hands are at his tie knot, not folding the collar (minor).
Notes frequent; kinpira and shodan notes longer than needed.
'That I kept them waiting' pronoun switch feels coy.
Nanoha switches 'Kohei' to 'Ko-chan' within one scene; made the reader pause.
'She noticed the squeaky stairs. Both of them.' is garbled and a weak setup.
Fog/modern-sword prologue has no callback in two chapters.
Horror-movie self-intro reads like a profile-card trait.
'Does Fujisawa ever compete up north?' is a mechanical on-ramp.
'Then + comic reframe' comeback spread across four characters (voice bleed).
Ryosuke and Takatsuki occupy the same pedant niche.
Nanoha and Natsuki share a dry deadpan register.
Kohei's spoken lines alone wouldn't always identify him (close to Kirishima).
Taiyaki glossed again in part 5 after a full note in part 2; redundant.
'Head first or tail first?': a reader might think she overheard Tokiwa's argument.
Several bare '[Natsuki appears on screen]' lines are noise.
Mountain small talk is generic filler while the good material sits in narrated summary.

Pronoun confusion: 'she' grammatically refers to Rika.
'I show her men' is unexplained kendo jargon until Takatsuki's line.
Natsuki's unexplained tear is a near-cliche hint, edge of too obvious.
Cedar pollen / 'It's April': the joke's premise may be wrong.

Lowercase internal-looking background label.

Nanoha on the wrong side relative to the river.

Hair and eye color never registered in the text.
Stutter gaze aimed away from Kohei's window seat.

Bandage already wound and stained while the text says she's winding it.

'Ryosuke' label and 'Tokiwa' narration are never explicitly linked.
'Drawer sticks' echo is too engineered.
'Since the first time I picked one up' is heavy-handed.
Nanoha's address wobble ('Kohei' then 'Ko-chan').
Six '[Natsuki appears on screen]' repeats; possible sprite churn.
Pronoun error: 'she' grammatically refers to Rika; fix with 'Mizuno'.
Translator-note pileup: 12 notes, 6 back to back before the match, duplicating inline glosses; hakama and kinpira notes long.
The unexplained tear is a stock device.
'...It's April' rebuttal is shaky.
Prologue untethered and coy (no text, no woman, never echoed).
Nanoha has no scene in Ch2, so the triangle tilts by absence; Ch2 needs a Nanoha scene with weight.
Bridge beat triple-explained (look at the river, c2_0224, the cup line).
'Is that the shrine?' is reader-facing exposition; she already knows.
'Right. You told me.' assumes an off-screen conversation; reads like a continuity slip.
Raw '[Background: natsuki apartment, night]' tag looks like a placeholder.
Ryosuke and Takatsuki overlap (both pedantic correctors).
Nanoha and Natsuki overlap in deadpan-tease mode.
Kohei sometimes too terse to have a voice in dialogue.
'Good morning, Tokiwa.' is dead air and stiff.
'Looking forward to this year.' is generic; the recovery after the stutter is lost.
'She's nice, Kohei. I like her.' restates the interlude.
Classmate lines are generic and interchangeable.
'Since I was little.' reads as nothing next to 'Kendo since I was seven'.
Takatsuki's 'It is the hardest thing in kendo to do on purpose.' is a pure explainer line.
'Okay. That's my project, then.' leaves it unclear what the project is; maybe too coy.
